symptom: `mxcli test --local` fails the build with `[CE0114] A microflow that does not apply entity access can only call microflows that also do not apply entity access. — at MxTest / Microflow 'RegisterEndpoint' / Call microflow activity '<your ASU>'` whenever the project's after-startup microflow applies entity access; no test runs, and the error says it is "in the project, not in this run's tests"
cause: `GenerateEndpointMDL` wrote `MxTest.RegisterEndpoint` without `@applyentityaccess`, so it did not apply entity access, and since the 2026-08 chaining fix it calls the project's after-startup microflow. `buildFailureHint` called every error not in a `Test_*` flow "in the project", including ones in the two documents the run itself generates
insight: Measure the rule's DIRECTION before choosing between mirroring the callee and a constant: with mx check on 11.13.0 (security Off and Production), non-applying -> applying is CE0114 while applying -> non-applying and applying -> applying are 0 errors (MDL-SEC22's table says the same for 11.14.0). So `@applyentityaccess` on the generated caller is compatible with every startup microflow, and needs no scrape of the user's flow — which the mirror fix would have added beside the DESCRIBE SETTINGS scrape that already broke once. The setting is neutral at runtime: it governs the caller's own activities only (a Java action ignores it), each callee runs with its own. Prove the chain still runs with a marker the test CONSUMES (`@cleanup none` + delete): a plain count passed on an earlier boot's marker under --skip-app-startup, i.e. the control could not fail. Generated documents with fixed names (RegisterEndpoint, RegisterTestEndpoint) are attributable exactly like the Test_* flows; say so and offer --skip-app-startup as the escape hatch
